svg.text: CN0565 · EIT — how every layer connects
Left = what you assume. Right = what the machine does. Red = a place the two must agree, and currently may not.
Every box carries the file:line that proves it. pyeit 1.2.4 · pyadi-iio 0.0.22 · pylibiio 0.25 · measured on this machine
BRANCH A · THE MODEL — pure simulation, no hardware, computed once
BRANCH B · THE MACHINE — real electrodes, real tissue, every frame
A1 · Mesh — the medium you ASSUME
Defines Ω and the conductivity field the solver believes in.
knobs: n_el · fd (boundary shape) · h0 · p_fix
default boundary = a circle; default σ = 1.0, dimensionless
mesh/wrapper.py:313 fd: Callable = shape.circle
mesh/wrapper.py:44 perm default_factory = 1.0
YOU CAN EDIT
A2 · Protocol — drive / read pattern
Which pair injects, which pair reads, and in what order.
knobs: dist_exc · step_meas · parser_meas
pairs built as (i + dist) % n_el — assumes a CLOSED RING
eit/protocol.py:310 (upstream :304)
measured: 16 exc × 13 meas = 208 values per frame
YOU CAN EDIT
A3 · FEM forward solve
current enters at ONE NODE: no contact impedance, no electrode area
eit/fem.py:90 b[el_pos[ex_line]] = [1, -1]
eit/fem.py:85 "only simple electrode model is supported"
σ is a SCALAR per element — anisotropic muscle cannot be expressed
eit/fem.py:405 data = ke[i] * perm[i]
EDITABLE — with structural limits
A4 · Jacobian J
Jᵢⱼ = ∂vᵢ/∂σⱼ J[i,:,e] = rᵢ Kₑ fₑ
eit/fem.py:223 (upstream :255)
measured on your config (16 el, h0=0.08):
J = 208 × 1083 · 5.21× underdetermined · cond = 1.34×10¹⁵
numerically singular — regularization is what makes a solution exist
YOU CAN EDIT
A5 · H — the reconstruction matrix
JAC H = (JᵀJ + λR)⁻¹ Jᵀ , R = diag(diag(JᵀJ))ᵖ
GREIT H = WᵀJᵀ(JJᵀ + λR)⁻¹ BP H = Bᵀ
eit/jac.py:93 + :103 · greit.py:118 · bp.py:56 (same upstream)
eit/jac.py:79 source cites "adler-dai-lionheart-2007"
knobs: p · lamb · method · solver choice
measured: sensitivity spread diag(JᵀJ) = 3091× rim vs centre
p=0 → 1× (noise to rim) · p=0.5 → 55.6× · p=1 → 3091× (to centre)

examples/cn0565/main.py · cn0565_worker.py · realtimeEITUI.py
working knobs: value_type (Re/Im/|Z|) · solver · baseline
BUG — the p and λ sliders are not connected to anything
worker.py:87,91 write self.pVal / self.lambdaVal → 0 reads anywhere
worker.py:160,172 pass literals p=0.5, lamb=0.01

worker.py:146 solver() called in while-loop → :158 rebuilds JAC,
recomputing FEM + Jacobian + inv(1083×1083) on every frame

B2 · pyadi-iio driver
site-packages/adi/{cn0565, ad5940, adg2128}.py
knobs: excitation_frequency · excitation_amplitude
electrode_count · force_distance · sense_distance
the LIVE copy is in site-packages, not work/upstream-download/
pyadi_iio-0.0.22.dist-info/direct_url.json → installed from a .zip,
not an editable install — edits to the extracted tree do nothing
YOU CAN EDIT
B3 · libiio + UART transport
site-packages/iio.py (ctypes) → libiio.dll → COM port
uri = "serial:COM7,230400,8n1"
iio.py:32 CDLL · iio.py:287 iio_create_context_from_uri
iio.py:1328 Context.__init__ calls _new_uri(uri)
measured: pylibiio 0.25, binding (0, 26, 'a0eca0d')
REFERENCE LIBRARY
B4 · Firmware (no-OS) — the ceiling, and it IS editable
Source is public: no-OS/projects/cn0565 (variants: eit, eit_iio)
your .hex name decodes exactly: cn0565 · eit_iio · eval-adicup3029
It publishes exactly FIVE device attributes — that is the ceiling:
iio_ad5940.c:236 impedance_mode :242 magnitude_mode
:248 excitation_frequency :254 excitation_amplitude
:260 gpio1_toggle :281 raw (channel 'bia')
pyadi-iio exposes those five and nothing else — a 1:1 match.
AppBiaCfg_Type already holds ~20 more knobs, just not published:
HstiaRtiaSel (RTIA 200Ω–160k) · DftNum · HanWinEn · BiaODR
ADCPgaGain · ADCSinc2/3Osr · SweepCfg (multi-frequency!) · RcalVal
bia_measurement.h AppBiaCfg_Type
Rebuild: python tools/scripts/no_os_build.py build
--project cn0565 --variant eit_iio --board eval-adicup3029
projects/cn0565/README.rst, Build Command · needs CCES installed
Then flash the new .hex the same way you already did: drag to DAPLINK.
EDITABLE — source is public, needs CCES + reflash
AD5940 drives AC excitation, runs a DFT, returns complex Z.
|Z| = (|Vₘₐᵍ| / |Iₘₐᵍ|) × R_TIA
CN-0565 circuit note Rev.A p.4, eq. (5)
ADG2128 routes F+/S+/S−/F− to any electrode (Fig. 10).
R_TIA has 20% tolerance and must be calibrated (p.5)
FIXED SILICON
The two branches meet — and this is the only place they touch
ds = − H · dv dv = (v1 − v0) / |v0|
eit/base.py:126 · eit/base.py:188 (identical upstream)
H comes from the left. dv comes from the right. Row i of J must be the same measurement as element i of dv.
Δσ image
sim2pts() → tripcolor() · GREIT: mask_value() → imshow() — a CHANGE, never an absolute tissue value
THE MEDIUM — what is actually between the electrodes?
Branch A assumes this. Branch B measures it. Everything above is only as true as these two agreeing.
Impedance test board
A lumped RC network. There is no spatial
conductivity field at all, so an EIT image of it
carries no anatomy — it only proves the data path.
Proof: it PASSED prod_tst, which checks fixed
R/C values, not any distribution.
Saline tank phantom
Circular, homogeneous, isotropic, closed ring of
electrodes — matches pyEIT's default model exactly.
This is the only configuration today where an
image can be trusted, and the only way to settle
cross-link 2 below.
Facial muscle
Open domain (current escapes into the head) · no
closed ring · layered skin/fat/bone/air · anisotropic
muscle · large contact impedance · and the electrodes
MOVE with the very expression you are imaging.
Every one of these breaks an assumption in A1–A3.
The connections — and the evidence for each
n_el is declared in three places
driver electrode_count · mesh n_el · protocol n_el. pyEIT only WARNS on mismatch, it does not stop you. proof: eit/fem.py:143–153
Driver and pyEIT label the sense electrodes in opposite order — on all 208 rows
208/208 same excitation pair, 208/208 same sense pair, 208/208 S+/S− swapped. proof: adi/cn0565.py:73–88 vs protocol.py:254–267 + fem.py:363
The p and λ sliders do nothing, and setup() reruns every frame
self.pVal / self.lambdaVal / self.reSetup: 0 reads. proof: cn0565_worker.py:87–96 vs :160, :172; :146 calls solver() inside the loop
Firmware sets the ceiling — but you can raise the ceiling yourself
5 attributes published (iio_ad5940.c:236–281) = exactly the 5 pyadi-iio exposes. To add one: enum + entry in the iio_attribute array + a case in get/set_attr, rebuild, reflash.
The fidelity gap — A1's assumed medium vs the real one
H is built entirely from the left column. Any mismatch is not flagged; it is rendered as a confident coloured blob.
excitation_frequency decides which tissue the current travels through
at 10 kHz the skin barrier dominates; membranes are largely invisible. AD5940 supports 0.015 Hz – 200 kHz. proof: CN-0565 Rev.A p.3
Electrode movement enters as perfectly valid data
the solver cannot distinguish it from Δσ. Adler 2009 trains GREIT against it — but pyEIT's GREIT is the 'dist' approximation, without that training. proof: greit.py:77–99
